definitions.meaning: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, pictured as an arrow: the arrow for (2, 3) moves 2 right and 3 up.
The length of the vector arrow: for (x, y) it is sqrt(x^2 + y^2) by Pythagoras, so |(2, 3)| = sqrt(13).
The record of a vector as its components stacked in a column: the top entry is the right move and the bottom entry is the up move, as in 2 over 3.
The scalar a . b = |a||b| cos theta, computed component by component; it measures how much of b points along a, and it is zero exactly when the vectors are perpendicular.
The vector of a point measured from the origin: it is pinned to the origin, so moving the point changes its position vector.
A free vector that gives the direction of a line or plane edge: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same direction vector, as in r = a + lambda b.

mechanismSteps: A vector has size and direction: the arrow moves 2 right and 3 up, its column vector records 2 over 3, and the length of the arrow is its magnitude.
Adding vectors: tail to head: place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first, and the sum runs from the very first tail to the very last head.
The dot product measures the shadow: drop a perpendicular from the tip of b onto a, and the projection is measured by a . b = |a||b| cos theta.
Lines and planes from a point and directions: one point plus one direction draws a line, r = a + lambda b; a plane needs two directions and its normal stands perpendicular to the whole surface.
A common mistake: moving a vector changes it: sliding a free vector to a new start point leaves it unchanged - only position vectors are pinned to the origin.
objectives: Describe a vector by its magnitude and direction, and write it as a column vector
Define the key vocabulary of vectors: vector, magnitude, column vector, dot product, position vector and direction vector
Add vectors tail to head, evaluate a dot product, and write vector equations of lines and planes

title: JC H2 vectors: direction, dot products, lines and planes

trap.explanation: Position vectors are pinned to the origin, so every vector feels pinned. Free vectors slide: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same vector. Only position vectors are pinned to the origin.
trap.misconception: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it.

workedExample: Take the arrow for the vector (2, 3): it moves 2 right and 3 up. Draw exactly the same arrow again starting at a new start point - still 2 right and 3 up - and it is the same vector: sliding it did not change its magnitude sqrt(13) or its direction. Only a position vector would change, because a position vector is pinned to the origin.
